title: Design of a Quantum Walk Circuit to Solve the Subset-Sum Problem
problem: Design an efficient quantum circuit implementing quantum walk search on Johnson graphs to solve the subset-sum problem, with detailed quantification of gate count, circuit depth, and qubit width requirements.
motivation: Quantum walk-based search algorithms provide potential computational speedup for combinatorial optimization and cryptography, but require practical circuit implementations with manageable resource costs.
method: Implements a quantum walk search algorithm on Johnson graph structures with detailed design of each sub-circuit component. Quantifies circuit costs in gate number, depth, and width. Compares against Grover's quantum search algorithm, demonstrating reductions in T-count and T-depth metrics for practically solvable problems.
key_novelty: Complete practical circuit implementation of quantum walk search on Johnson graphs with detailed cost analysis, filling the gap between theoretical complexity analyses and implementable quantum circuits.
contributions: Complete implementation of quantum walk search on Johnson graphs for subset-sum problem
Detailed sub-circuit designs with quantified costs (gate count, circuit depth, qubit width)
Comparison with Grover's algorithm showing T-count and T-depth reduction
Reusable building block for efficient quantum search algorithms on Johnson graph structures

metrics.other: T-count and T-depth reduction versus Grover search

limitations: Paper focuses on practically solvable problem instances but does not discuss scalability to larger problem sizes or computational complexity limits.
primary_theme: Quantum walk circuits for subset-sum optimization
